quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Keep your eyes focused on the front of the motorcycle.
Look ahead to where you want to go through the turn.
Turn your whole body to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead to where you want to go through the turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: A major effect of drinking alcohol is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slowed body functions.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down your body and mind, affecting both physical and mental abilities.

questions.question: To lower the chance of a crash, you should do all of the following except:

options.text: Be ready to react to hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope another driver sees you.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use clear signals to show what you plan to do. Keep space between you and other vehicles. Watch for hazards and be ready to react.

questions.question: A face shield should:

options.text: Give you a clear view to both sides.
Block all air from passing through.
Be tight enough so glasses cannot fit under it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a clear view to both sides.
questions.explanation: A good face shield should have no scratches, resist damage, allow clear views to both sides, fasten securely, allow air to pass through, and have enough room for glasses if needed.

questions.question: Group riders should avoid riding side-by-side because:

options.text: A driver pulling in may not see both riders.
Helmet reflections may block the riders' vision.
Side-by-side riding does not give riders enough space to move around hazards.
It is too hard for left-side riders to exit the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side-by-side riding does not give riders enough space to move around hazards.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, do not ride side-by-side. Neither rider will have enough room to maneuver and avoid hazards.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher is legally intoxicated.
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: For people 21 and older, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means you are legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to operate a motorcycle while intoxicated.

questions.question: When someone follows you too closely, you should:

options.text: Ignore them and focus on the road ahead.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only make them follow even closer at a higher speed. Never ride on the shoulder because other drivers will not expect you there.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is well-protected when wearing:

options.text: Shoes that stop below the ankle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather gloves.
questions.explanation: For protection, wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs. Wear sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. Choose footwear with low heels that will not catch on foot pegs. Leather gloves protect your hands in a crash and give you a better grip on the controls.

questions.question: When a vehicle passes you on your left, you should:

options.text: Move as far right as possible to help them pass.
Move to the shoulder to help them pass.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Riding toward the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding away from them may cause them to move back into your lane too soon. Stay centered in your lane.

questions.question: An advantage of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles is:

options.text: You can pass danger more quickly.
You will have a narrow view of the road to stay focused.
You will have more time to react to other drivers' movements.
You can more easily follow the next vehicle's path.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to react to other drivers' movements.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles gives you a better view of hazards, more time to react, and more room to move around them.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After at least an hour of riding.
After more than 8 hours of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles. They occur just a few minutes after the rider starts riding.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get out of the wobble.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce speed.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble. This will make it worse. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly and slow down gradually. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not use the brakes hard, as this can also make the wobble worse.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Slow down to approach the dog, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to approach the dog, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, shift to a lower gear and slow down to get close to the dog. Once you are near it, speed up and leave it behind. Do not try to kick the dog.

questions.question: Use your mirrors when stopped at an intersection to:

options.text: See if parked cars are entering traffic.
Check for vehicles behind you that may not be stopping.
See if someone plans to turn behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for vehicles behind you that may not be stopping.
questions.explanation: When stopped at an intersection, use your mirrors to watch for cars coming up behind you. The drivers may not see you until they are very close. You may need to react quickly.

questions.question: Riders without helmets are ________ to die in a crash than riders with helmets.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times as likely
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders with helmets. This is true no matter what speed you are riding.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the left handgrip
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is usually located on the left handgrip of a motorcycle.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo:

options.text: It takes less time to accelerate but more time to stop.
It takes more time to accelerate and stop.
It takes more time to accelerate but less time to stop.
It takes less time to accelerate and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes more time to accelerate and stop.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from cargo or a passenger makes motorcycles take longer to speed up and slow down.

questions.question: A motorcyclist's cushion of space:

options.text: Should change based on riding conditions.
Is not needed in most situations.
Should be avoided to keep traffic moving safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should change based on riding conditions.
questions.explanation: Increase your space cushion when your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Do this on slippery pavement, when you cannot see ahead, or when traffic is heavy and other drivers may cut in front of you.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards and conditions.

questions.question: A skidding rear tire:

options.text: Removes your ability to change direction.
Is only a problem if the front tire is also skidding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Removes your ability to change direction.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is very dangerous and can cause a violent crash with serious injury or death. Too much rear brake pressure locks the rear wheel. When the rear wheel locks, you cannot steer. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This way, they won't fall behind, and experienced riders can watch them from behind.

questions.question: What should you do if you must ride over an obstacle?

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Stay seated and remove your feet from the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down before hitting the obstacle. Approach it at a 90-degree angle if you can. Keep your motorcycle upright. Just before you hit it, ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: What should you do if a dog chases you?

options.text: Stop until the animal loses interest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Dogs are often attracted to motorcycles. If chased by a dog, slow down and approach it. Then speed up to leave it behind.

questions.question: Which item provides the best protection for a rider?
questions.correctAnswerText: A face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield and eyeglasses do not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when you need more space to stop. Also increase it in heavy traffic or when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead.
